newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close down, ending series of records.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close down, ending series of records.

text.p: Dutch shares broke with their recent series of record closes on Wednesday with the main AEX index losing 8.70 points to end at 618.40.
Volumes picked up and prices sank further at the end of the session, as players were disappointed by U.S. economic data.
But dealers said this was no more than a healthy correction to the powerful rally which Dutch shares have staged this year.
One dealer said he did not expect the index to go below 600.
"There is still so much money from pension funds and investment funds waiting to be invested in the Netherlands that any correction won't go very far," he said.

Royal Dutch lost 5.30 guilders at 287.40 on weaker crude oil prices and a technical reaction to the stock's recent strength. One dealer said the stock could fall as far as 270.00, but another one saw support at 280.00

Nedlloyd, which reported lower third quarter profits, was unable to maintain initial gains and closed down 1.60 at 44.20 guilders. "The results were fine, but the forecast was much less bright," one dealer said.
Retailer Ahold disappointed the market despite higher third-quarter earnings. The shares closed 3.40 guilders lower at 102.90.
